source.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא חָלָ֖ה אֲבִיָּ֥ה בֶן־יָרָבְעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: At the time the that became sick Abijah [the] son of Jeroboam.

en.L: At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam became sick.
en.B: At that time Abijah son of Jeroboam fell ill.
en.R: Around that time Jeroboam's son Abijah became sick.

decisions.choice: at that time: in the days of Jeroboam's reign just told
decisions.reason: The phrase links this story loosely to the events of chapters 12-13, after Jeroboam set up his own places of worship and would not turn from his way (13:33-34). It does not give an exact date.

decisions.choice: Abijah: a name meaning "my father is Yahweh"
decisions.reason: Even the son of the king who set up the calves at Bethel and Dan bears a name that confesses Yahweh. He is a different person from Rehoboam's son Abijam (verse 31), who is called Abijah in 2 Chronicles 12:16.

decisions.choice: became sick: the illness that opens the word of judgment
decisions.reason: The prophet Ahijah had promised Jeroboam a lasting house if he obeyed (11:38). The sickness of his son becomes the occasion for that promise to be withdrawn (verses 7-16).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יָרָבְעָ֜ם לְאִשְׁתּ֗וֹ ק֤וּמִי נָא֙ וְהִשְׁתַּנִּ֔ית וְלֹ֣א יֵֽדְע֔וּ כִּי־אַ֖תְּ אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֑ם וְהָלַ֣כְתְּ שִׁלֹ֗ה הִנֵּה־שָׁם֙ אֲחִיָּ֣ה הַנָּבִ֔יא הֽוּא־דִבֶּ֥ר עָלַ֛י לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jeroboam to his wife, arise please and disguise yourself, and not they will know that you [are the] wife of Jeroboam, and you will go [to] Shiloh; behold there [is] Ahijah the prophet; he spoke about me to [be] king over the people the this.

en.L: And Jeroboam said to his wife, "Arise, please, and disguise yourself, so that they will not know that you [are the] wife of Jeroboam, and go to Shiloh. Look, Ahijah the prophet [is] there; he [is the one who] spoke about me, [that I would be] king over this people.
en.B: Jeroboam told his wife, "Please get up and change your appearance, so that no one will recognize you are Jeroboam's wife, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there, the one who told me that I would be king over this people.
en.R: Jeroboam said to his wife, "Please get ready and dress so that no one will know you are my wife. Then go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet lives there. He is the one who told me that I would become king of this people.

decisions.choice: Ahijah the prophet who spoke about me: the prophet of 11:29-39
decisions.reason: Ahijah of Shiloh had met Jeroboam outside Jerusalem, torn his new cloak into twelve pieces and given him ten, promising him the kingdom of ten tribes (11:29-31). Jeroboam sends to the prophet who once spoke for him.

decisions.choice: disguise yourself, so that they will not know: the reason is concealment
decisions.reason: The verb means to change oneself, to make oneself look different (1 Samuel 28:8 uses a related word for Saul). "They will not know" has no named subject: no one, neither the people on the way nor the prophet himself, is to recognize her. The text does not say why Jeroboam wants this, but he had turned away from the word Ahijah brought (11:38; 13:33).

decisions.choice: Shiloh: the old shrine town in the hill country of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Shiloh was where the tent of meeting stood in the days of Joshua and Eli (Joshua 18:1; 1 Samuel 1:3). It lay in Jeroboam's own northern kingdom, a day's journey or so from his capital.

decisions.choice: Ahijah the prophet is there (Balanced); Ahijah the prophet lives there (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "behold" points out where Ahijah is to be found; Balanced and Readable say this with a plain statement. The speech runs on into verse 3, so its closing quote mark is there.

source.text: וְלָקַ֣חַתְּ בְּ֠יָדֵךְ עֲשָׂרָ֨ה לֶ֧חֶם וְנִקֻּדִ֛ים וּבַקְבֻּ֥ק דְּבַ֖שׁ וּבָ֣את אֵלָ֑יו ה֚וּא יַגִּ֣יד לָ֔ךְ מַה־יִּֽהְיֶ֖ה לַנָּֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take in your hand ten bread[s] and cakes and a jar of honey, and you will go to him; he will tell you what will be to the boy.

en.L: And take in your hand ten [loaves of] bread and cakes and a jar of honey, and go to him; he will tell you what will happen to the boy."
en.B: Go to him with ten loaves of bread in your hand, some cakes and a jar of honey. He will tell you what is going to happen to the boy."
en.R: Take him ten loaves of bread, some cakes and a jar of honey. He will tell you what is going to happen to our son."

decisions.choice: ten loaves, cakes and a jar of honey: a gift for the prophet
decisions.reason: People who came to ask a prophet or seer for a word brought a gift (1 Samuel 9:7-8; 2 Kings 8:8-9). This is a plain household gift, the kind an ordinary woman might bring, not a king's present, which suits the disguise.

decisions.choice: cakes: small baked cakes, perhaps crumbly or marked with dots
decisions.reason: The word is rare. In Joshua 9:5, 12 it describes dry, crumbled bread; here it seems to be a kind of small biscuit or cake, perhaps named for its speckled surface.

decisions.choice: the boy: the king's young son
decisions.reason: The word can mean a boy or a young man; verse 12 calls him "the child". He was still young enough to live in his parents' house.

decisions.choice: our son (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable has Jeroboam speak of the boy as "our son", since the speaker and the hearer are his parents.

source.text: וַתַּ֤עַשׂ כֵּן֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֔ם וַתָּ֨קָם֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶךְ שִׁלֹ֔ה וַתָּבֹ֖א בֵּ֣ית אֲחִיָּ֑ה וַאֲחִיָּ֨הוּ֙ לֹֽא־יָכֹ֣ל לִרְא֔וֹת כִּ֛י קָ֥מוּ עֵינָ֖יו מִשֵּׂיבֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And did so [the] wife of Jeroboam, and she arose and went [to] Shiloh and came [to the] house of Ahijah; and Ahijah not was able to see, for were set his eyes from his old age.

en.L: And the wife of Jeroboam did so; and she arose and went to Shiloh and came to the house of Ahijah. And Ahijah was not able to see, for his eyes had become set because of his old age.
en.B: Jeroboam's wife did so. She set out for Shiloh and arrived at the house of Ahijah. Ahijah was unable to see; his eyes had grown fixed with age.
en.R: Jeroboam's wife did as he said. She went to Shiloh and came to Ahijah's house. Ahijah could not see, because he was very old and had become blind.

decisions.choice: his eyes had become set: he had become blind
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand or be fixed. Eyes that "stand" no longer move or see, the same phrase used for old Eli (1 Samuel 4:15).

decisions.choice: Ahijah could not see: the disguise was useless from the start
decisions.reason: The careful disguise was aimed at a man who could not see her at all, and Yahweh was about to tell him who she was (verse 5). The story sets human scheming against what Yahweh knows.

decisions.choice: had become blind (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states the plain sense of the idiom (m1).

source.text: וַיהוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אֲחִיָּ֗הוּ הִנֵּ֣ה אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֡ם בָּאָ֣ה לִדְרֹשׁ֩ דָּבָ֨ר מֵעִמְּךָ֤ אֶל־בְּנָהּ֙ כִּֽי־חֹלֶ֣ה ה֔וּא כָּזֹ֥ה וְכָזֶ֖ה תְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֑יהָ וִיהִ֣י כְבֹאָ֔הּ וְהִ֖יא מִתְנַכֵּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Yahweh said to Ahijah, behold [the] wife of Jeroboam [is] coming to seek a word from you about her son, for sick [is] he; like this and like this you will speak to her; and it will be when she comes, and she [will be] making herself a stranger.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to Ahijah, "Look, the wife of Jeroboam [is] coming to seek a word from you about her son, for he [is] sick. Thus and thus you shall speak to her. And it will be, when she comes, that she [will be] making herself [out to be] a stranger."
en.B: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you for a word about her son, because he is sick. You are to tell her such and such. When she arrives, she will be pretending to be someone else."
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had already spoken to Ahijah. He said, "Jeroboam's wife is coming to ask you what will happen to her son, because he is sick. You must tell her what I tell you. When she comes, she will be pretending to be another woman."

decisions.choice: Yahweh had said: before she arrived
decisions.reason: The clause begins with the subject, a way Hebrew marks background. Yahweh had spoken to Ahijah before the woman reached his door.

decisions.choice: to seek a word: to ask a prophet for a message from God
decisions.reason: To "seek" or "inquire" of a prophet was to come to him for Yahweh's answer on a matter (1 Samuel 9:9; 2 Kings 8:8).

decisions.choice: thus and thus you shall speak: the storyteller shortens Yahweh's message
decisions.reason: "Like this and like this" stands for the words Yahweh gave Ahijah, which the reader hears in full in verses 6-16. The narrator does not repeat them here.

decisions.choice: making herself a stranger: pretending to be someone else
decisions.reason: The verb means to act as a stranger, to make oneself unrecognized. She will act as if she were some other woman.

decisions.choice: tell her what I tell you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "thus and thus" (m3); an English reader would find "such and such" puzzling. Readable also adds "He said" to start the speech, with "He" for Yahweh.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲחִיָּ֜הוּ אֶת־ק֤וֹל רַגְלֶ֨יהָ֙ בָּאָ֣ה בַפֶּ֔תַח וַיֹּ֕אמֶר בֹּ֖אִי אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֑ם לָ֣מָּה זֶּ֗ה אַ֚תְּ מִתְנַכֵּרָ֔ה וְאָ֣נֹכִ֔י שָׁל֥וּחַ אֵלַ֖יִךְ קָשָֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was as heard Ahijah the sound of her feet coming in the doorway, and he said, come in, [the] wife of Jeroboam; why this [that] you [are] making yourself a stranger? and I [am] sent to you [with] hard [news].

en.L: And it happened, as Ahijah heard the sound of her feet coming in at the doorway, that he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why [is] this, [that] you [are] making yourself [out to be] a stranger? I [am] sent to you [with] hard [news].
en.B: As soon as Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps at the doorway, he said, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why are you pretending to be someone else? I have been sent to you with hard news.
en.R: Ahijah heard her footsteps as she reached the doorway. At once he called out, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam. Why are you pretending to be someone else? I have been sent to give you bad news.

decisions.choice: Come in, wife of Jeroboam: the blind prophet names her at once
decisions.reason: Before she says a word, Ahijah greets her by who she is. What Yahweh had told him (verse 5) shows that the disguise could not hide her.

decisions.choice: I am sent to you with hard news: a heavy, harsh message
decisions.reason: The adjective means hard or severe; the noun "news" or "word" is understood. "Sent" marks Ahijah as Yahweh's messenger: the word is not his own.

decisions.choice: [with] hard [news] (Literal); with hard news (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Hebrew says only "hard"; English supplies the noun. Ahijah's speech runs to verse 16, where its closing quote mark is.

decisions.choice: bad news (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday phrase for a hard message.

source.text: לְכִ֞י אִמְרִ֣י לְיָרָבְעָ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יַ֛עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲרִימֹתִ֖יךָ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָעָ֑ם וָאֶתֶּנְךָ֣ נָגִ֔יד עַ֖ל עַמִּ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Go say to Jeroboam, thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel, because that I raised you from among the people and I made you ruler over my people Israel,

en.L: Go, say to Jeroboam, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel,
en.B: Go and tell Jeroboam, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.
en.R: Go and tell Jeroboam, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: I lifted you up from among the ordinary people and made you the leader of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel.

decisions.choice: because: the start of a charge that runs through verse 9
decisions.reason: Yahweh's message has the form of a prophet's judgment: first the reasons ("because ...", verses 7-9), then the sentence ("therefore ...", verse 10).

decisions.choice: I raised you up from among the people: Jeroboam owed his rise to Yahweh
decisions.reason: Jeroboam was a servant of Solomon, the son of a widow, and a man of no royal family (11:26-28). The same words were spoken of David (1 Samuel 13:14; 2 Samuel 7:8) and are later spoken to Baasha (16:2).

decisions.choice: ruler: the one Yahweh appoints over his people
decisions.reason: This title (nagid) is used for Saul, David and Solomon as leaders appointed by Yahweh (1 Samuel 9:16; 2 Samuel 7:8; 1 Kings 1:35). It stresses that the people are Yahweh's, and the ruler serves under him.

decisions.choice: the "because" clause is broken into statements (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs from here to verse 10. Balanced and Readable state each charge as its own sentence, and "therefore" in verse 10 still gives the sentence that follows from them (m1). The message to Jeroboam is in single quote marks, inside Ahijah's speech, and closes at the end of verse 11.

decisions.choice: the leader (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for nagid in these books: "ruler" at Literal and Balanced, "leader" at Readable.

source.text: וָאֶקְרַ֤ע אֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ מִבֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד וָאֶתְּנֶ֖הָ לָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא־הָיִ֜יתָ כְּעַבְדִּ֣י דָוִ֗ד אֲשֶׁר֩ שָׁמַ֨ר מִצְוֺתַ֜י וַאֲשֶׁר־הָלַ֤ךְ אַחֲרַי֙ בְּכָל־לְבָב֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת רַ֖ק הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I tore the kingdom from [the] house of David and gave it to you; and not you have been like my servant David who kept my commandments and who walked after me with all his heart, to do only the right in my eyes,

en.L: and I tore the kingdom from the house of David and gave it to you; but you have not been like {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave David, who kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments and who walked after {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all his heart, to do only what [was] right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes,
en.B: I tore the kingdom out of the hands of David's house and gave it to you. Yet you have not been like {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David, who kept {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments, who followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} wholeheartedly and did nothing but what was right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight.
en.R: I took the kingdom away from David's family and gave it to you. But you have not been like {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant David. He obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands and followed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all his heart. He did only what I consider right.

decisions.choice: I tore the kingdom from the house of David: the torn cloak of 11:29-31
decisions.reason: Ahijah had torn his cloak to show that Yahweh would tear the kingdom from Solomon's hand (11:11, 31). The kingdom passed to Jeroboam as a gift from Yahweh, not as his own winning.

decisions.choice: like my servant David: David as the measure of a king
decisions.reason: Kings measures every later king against David, who did not turn to other gods (11:4, 6, 33, 38; 15:3, 11). This does not deny David's sins; 15:5 names the matter of Uriah. The point is his undivided loyalty to Yahweh. Jeroboam had been promised a lasting house if he walked as David did (11:38).

decisions.choice: walked after me: followed Yahweh as one follows a master
decisions.reason: To walk after someone is to follow and serve them. Its opposite is to "go after" other gods (11:10).

decisions.choice: my slave David (Literal); my servant David (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for "my servant David" in these books, following the rule for this word.

decisions.choice: what I consider right (Readable)
decisions.reason: "In my eyes" means in Yahweh's judgment; Readable says this plainly, and the pronoun "I" needs no setting.

source.text: וַתָּ֣רַע לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁר־הָי֣וּ לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַתֵּ֡לֶךְ וַתַּעֲשֶׂה־לְּךָ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים אֲחֵרִ֤ים וּמַסֵּכוֹת֙ לְהַכְעִיסֵ֔נִי וְאֹתִ֥י הִשְׁלַ֖כְתָּ אַחֲרֵ֥י גַוֶּֽךָ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you have done evil to act more than all who were before you, and you went and made for yourself other gods and cast images to provoke me to anger, and me you have thrown behind your back,

en.L: and you have done evil more than all who were before you, and you have gone and made for yourself other gods and cast images to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger, and {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you have thrown behind your back,
en.B: You have done more evil than all who were before you. You went and made yourself other gods, images of cast metal, to provoke {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to anger, and you have thrown {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} behind your back.
en.R: You have done more evil than all who ruled before you. You made other gods for yourself, idols of melted metal, and so you have made {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} angry. You have turned your back on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and thrown {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} aside.

decisions.choice: more than all who were before you: worse than any leader of Israel before him
decisions.reason: Before Jeroboam, Israel's kings were Saul, David and Solomon; the phrase may also take in the judges. Even Solomon's turning to other gods (11:5-8) is outdone by a king who made idols the center of the nation's worship. The same phrase is later used of other kings (16:25, 30).

decisions.choice: other gods and cast images: the golden calves of Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: Jeroboam made two calves of gold and told the people, "Here are your gods, Israel" (12:28-29). The word "cast image" is the word used for the golden calf at Sinai (Exodus 32:4, 8), and the law forbids such images (Exodus 34:17). Yahweh calls them "other gods" even if Jeroboam meant them to stand for him.

decisions.choice: you have thrown me behind your back: you have rejected me with contempt
decisions.reason: To throw something behind one's back is to put it out of sight and mind, to treat it as worthless (Ezekiel 23:35; Nehemiah 9:26). The Hebrew puts "me" first for emphasis.

decisions.choice: to provoke me to anger: to stir Yahweh to righteous anger
decisions.reason: This phrase recurs throughout Kings for worship of idols (verse 15; 15:30; 16:2). It describes deliberate offense, as if done to provoke.

decisions.choice: turned your back on me and thrown me aside (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m3) in common words.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֤יא רָעָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יָרָבְעָ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י לְיָֽרָבְעָם֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֔יר עָצ֥וּר וְעָז֖וּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבִֽעַרְתִּי֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית־יָרָבְעָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יְבַעֵ֥ר הַגָּלָ֖ל עַד־תֻּמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore behold I [am] bringing evil to [the] house of Jeroboam, and I will cut off from Jeroboam one urinating against a wall, restrained and left free in Israel; and I will burn up after [the] house of Jeroboam just as one burns up the dung until its finishing.

en.L: therefore, look, I [am] bringing evil on the house of Jeroboam, and I will cut off from Jeroboam [every] one who urinates against a wall, bond and free, in Israel, and I will burn up after the house of Jeroboam as one burns up the dung, until it is finished.
en.B: Therefore I am about to bring disaster on Jeroboam's house. From Jeroboam I will cut off every male in Israel, bond or free. I will burn away what remains of his house, the way someone burns up dung until none is left.
en.R: So I am going to bring disaster on Jeroboam's family. I will destroy every man and boy in Jeroboam's family in Israel, slave or free. I will get rid of his family completely, the way a person burns up dung until nothing is left.

decisions.choice: one who urinates against a wall: a male
decisions.reason: This coarse phrase means a male, from the boy upward, and is used in threats to wipe out every male of a household (1 Samuel 25:22, 34; 1 Kings 16:11; 21:21; 2 Kings 9:8). The coarse words also show contempt.

decisions.choice: restrained and left free: everyone, whatever his standing
decisions.reason: The pair of words is a fixed expression for "everyone" (Deuteronomy 32:36; 1 Kings 21:21; 2 Kings 9:8; 14:26), but what each half means is not certain. It may mean slave and free, someone kept at home and someone free to go out, a minor and an adult, or someone under protection and someone left on his own. Whichever it is, the pair covers every male without exception.

decisions.choice: I will burn up after the house of Jeroboam as one burns up the dung: a complete and contemptuous removal
alternatives: I will sweep away the house of Jeroboam as one sweeps away dung
decisions.reason: The verb means to burn, and also to sweep away or purge (Deuteronomy 13:6). "After" means what remains behind. The picture is either of dried dung burned as fuel until none is left, or of filth cleared away until the place is clean. Either way, the house of Jeroboam is treated as refuse and removed completely.

decisions.choice: every male (Balanced); every man and boy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the plain sense of the coarse idiom (m1), as 1 Samuel 25:22 does; Literal keeps its picture. No gender setting is used, because only males are meant.

decisions.choice: bond and free (Literal); bond or free (Balanced); slave or free (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the pair as a fixed expression close to its literal sense; Readable uses the most likely meaning (m2). All mean every male without exception, and the footnote gives the other possible senses. The same wording is used at 21:21.

decisions.choice: disaster (Balanced, Readable); evil (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means evil done or evil suffered. Here it is the harm Yahweh brings as punishment, not wrongdoing.

source.text: הַמֵּ֨ת לְיָֽרָבְעָ֤ם בָּעִיר֙ יֹאכְל֣וּ הַכְּלָבִ֔ים וְהַמֵּת֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה יֹאכְל֖וּ ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: The one dying of Jeroboam in the city will eat the dogs, and the one dying in the field will eat [the] birds of the heavens; for Yahweh has spoken.

en.L: The one belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and the one who dies in the field, the birds of the heavens will eat; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.'
en.B: Anyone belonging to Jeroboam who dies in the city, the dogs will eat, and anyone who dies in the open country, the birds of the sky will eat. For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.'
en.R: Dogs will eat anyone in Jeroboam's family who dies in the city, and birds will eat anyone who dies out in the country. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said this.'

decisions.choice: dogs will eat ... birds will eat: they will lie unburied
decisions.reason: To be left unburied, food for scavenging dogs and birds, was the worst disgrace and a sign of a curse (Deuteronomy 28:26; 1 Samuel 17:44, 46). Dogs in the towns of Israel were half-wild scavengers, not pets. The same sentence is spoken later against the houses of Baasha (16:4) and Ahab (21:24).

decisions.choice: the field: the open country outside the town
decisions.reason: The word means land outside the town walls, whether farmland or wild country. Together, "city" and "field" mean anywhere at all.

decisions.choice: for Yahweh has spoken: the seal on the message
decisions.reason: This closing phrase confirms that the sentence will surely be carried out (Isaiah 1:2; 22:25). It ends the message for Jeroboam that began in verse 7.

decisions.choice: the birds of the heavens (Literal); the birds of the sky (Balanced); birds (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "heavens" here is the sky where birds fly, as in 1 Samuel 17:44. The same wording is used for the houses of Baasha (16:4) and Ahab (21:24). The single quote mark closes the message Ahijah gives for Jeroboam (opened in verse 7); Ahijah's own speech to the woman continues.

source.text: וְאַ֥תְּ ק֖וּמִי לְכִ֣י לְבֵיתֵ֑ךְ בְּבֹאָ֥ה רַגְלַ֛יִךְ הָעִ֖ירָה וּמֵ֥ת הַיָּֽלֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you arise, go to your house; in [the] coming of your feet the city-ward, and will die the child.

en.L: And you, arise, go to your house; when your feet enter the city, the child will die.
en.B: As for you, get up and return to your house. The moment your feet enter the city, the child will die.
en.R: Now get up and go home. As soon as you step into the city, your child will die.

decisions.choice: and you: Ahijah turns from the message for Jeroboam to the woman herself
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first for emphasis. After the message she must carry to her husband (verses 7-11), Ahijah answers the question she came with (verse 3).

decisions.choice: when your feet enter the city, the child will die: the sign that the word is true
decisions.reason: The timing of the boy's death will show that Ahijah spoke for Yahweh (Deuteronomy 18:22). It happens exactly so in verse 17.

decisions.choice: as soon as you step into the city (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts "your feet enter" in everyday words.

source.text: וְסָֽפְדוּ־ל֤וֹ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְקָבְר֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ כִּֽי־זֶ֣ה לְבַדּ֔וֹ יָבֹ֥א לְיָרָבְעָ֖ם אֶל־קָ֑בֶר יַ֣עַן נִמְצָא־ב֞וֹ דָּבָ֣ר ט֗וֹב אֶל־יְהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּבֵ֥ית יָרָבְעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will mourn for him all Israel and bury him, for this [one] alone of Jeroboam will come to a grave, because was found in him a thing good toward Yahweh [the] God of Israel in [the] house of Jeroboam.

en.L: And all Israel will mourn for him and bury him, for this [one] alone of Jeroboam's will come to a grave, because in him was found something good toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam.
en.B: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He is the only one belonging to Jeroboam who will be laid in a grave, because in him something good toward {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has been found in the house of Jeroboam.
en.R: All the people of Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He will be the only one in Jeroboam's family to be buried in a grave. In all of Jeroboam's family, he is the only one in whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has found anything good.

decisions.choice: he alone will come to a grave: his early death is a mercy
decisions.reason: Every other male of Jeroboam's house will die by violence and lie unburied (verses 10-11). This boy alone will die at home, be mourned by the whole nation and receive an honorable burial (verse 18). His death spares him the end of his family.

decisions.choice: something good toward Yahweh: some goodness or faithfulness Yahweh saw in him
decisions.reason: The text does not say what the good thing was. It may have been the boy's own loyalty or disposition toward Yahweh. The point is the contrast with the rest of the house.

decisions.choice: In all of Jeroboam's family, he is the only one in whom the LORD has found anything good (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the passive "was found in him" into an active sentence with Yahweh as the one who finds, and brings "in the house of Jeroboam" forward to make the contrast clear.

source.text: וְהֵקִים֩ יְהוָ֨ה ל֥וֹ מֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַכְרִ֛ית אֶת־בֵּ֥ית יָרָבְעָ֖ם זֶ֣ה הַיּ֑וֹם וּמֶ֖ה גַּם־עָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will raise up Yahweh for himself a king over Israel who will cut off [the] house of Jeroboam this [is] the day; and what? even now.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will raise up for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} a king over Israel who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This [is] the day; and what? Even now.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will raise up a king of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own over Israel, and that king will cut off Jeroboam's house. This is the day; indeed, it has already begun.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will choose a king over Israel who will destroy Jeroboam's family. That day has come; in fact, it has already begun.

decisions.choice: a king who will cut off the house of Jeroboam: Baasha
decisions.reason: Baasha killed Jeroboam's son Nadab and struck down the whole house of Jeroboam, "according to the word of Yahweh that he spoke by the hand of his servant Ahijah" (15:27-30).

decisions.choice: this is the day; and what? even now: the judgment has already begun
alternatives: who will cut off the house of Jeroboam on that day; and what now? even now
this is the day! What am I saying? It is now
decisions.reason: These closing words are very short and hard to read. They seem to say that the day of judgment is not far off but already here, beginning with the boy's death. Other readings take them as "this is the day, and what [more]? Even now [it is happening]", or join "this day" to the cutting off ("who will cut off the house of Jeroboam on this day"). All of them stress how near the judgment is.

decisions.choice: indeed, it has already begun (Balanced); in fact, it has already begun (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the broken phrase "and what? even now" (m2). Literal keeps its bare form.

decisions.choice: a king of his own (Balanced); will choose a king (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "raise up for himself" in plainer words: Yahweh brings the king to power for his own purpose.

source.text: וְהִכָּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנ֣וּד הַקָּנֶה֮ בַּמַּיִם֒ וְנָתַ֣שׁ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מֵ֠עַל הָאֲדָמָ֨ה הַטּוֹבָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַן֙ לַאֲב֣וֹתֵיהֶ֔ם וְזֵרָ֖ם מֵעֵ֣בֶר לַנָּהָ֑ר יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ אֶת־אֲשֵׁ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם מַכְעִיסִ֖ים אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will strike Yahweh Israel as sways the reed in the water, and he will uproot Israel from on the ground the good the this which he gave to their fathers, and he will scatter them from beyond the River, because they made their Asherah poles provoking Yahweh to anger.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strike Israel as the reed sways in the water, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will uproot Israel from this good land that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to their fathers, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will strike Israel until it sways like a reed in the water. He will pull Israel up by the roots from this good land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave their ancestors and scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, because they have made their Asherah poles and provoked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to anger.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will strike Israel, and it will shake like a reed in a stream. He will pull Israel up by the roots out of this good land that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to their ancestors. He will scatter them to the far side of the Euphrates River. This is because they made poles used to worship Asherah and made {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} angry.

decisions.choice: as the reed sways in the water: Israel will be shaken and unstable
decisions.reason: A reed in a stream bends with every current and has no firm footing. The picture is of a nation tossed about by Yahweh's blows, never secure.

decisions.choice: uproot ... scatter them beyond the River: exile from the land
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Euphrates. Moses warned that if Israel turned to other gods, Yahweh would uproot them from the land (Deuteronomy 29:27) and scatter them among the nations (Deuteronomy 28:64). It happened when Assyria carried the northern kingdom away (2 Kings 17:6, 23).

decisions.choice: Asherah poles: wooden poles or trees set up to worship the goddess Asherah
decisions.reason: Asherah was a Canaanite goddess. Her sign was a wooden pole or tree set up beside an altar, which the law commanded Israel to cut down (Exodus 34:13; Deuteronomy 7:5; 16:21). The poles here are the first mention in Kings of this worship in the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: the River (Literal); the Euphrates River (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the river, as 2 Samuel 10:16 does (m2).

decisions.choice: poles used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for asherim in these books: "Asherah poles" at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וְיִתֵּ֖ן אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּגְלַ֞ל חַטֹּ֤אות יָֽרָבְעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will give up Israel on account of [the] sins of Jeroboam which he sinned and which he made sin Israel.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give up Israel on account of the sins of Jeroboam, which he sinned and which he made Israel sin."
en.B: He will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he committed and by which he led Israel to sin."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will abandon Israel because of the sins of Jeroboam. Jeroboam sinned, and he led Israel into sin as well."

decisions.choice: he will give up Israel: Yahweh will hand Israel over to its enemies
decisions.reason: The verb "give" here means to give up, abandon, hand over. Yahweh will no longer protect the people.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned and which he made Israel sin
decisions.reason: This phrase becomes the refrain of Kings for every northern king (15:26, 30, 34; 16:26; 2 Kings 17:21-22). Jeroboam's sin was not only his own: he led the whole nation into false worship at Bethel and Dan (12:30).

decisions.choice: The LORD will abandon Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names Yahweh as the subject, which the Hebrew verb leaves to be understood. The double quote mark closes Ahijah's speech, opened in verse 6.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin (Literal); led Israel to sin (Balanced); led Israel into sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: This phrase is said of nearly every king of Israel after Jeroboam (m2), and each level keeps one wording for it throughout Kings: "made Israel sin" at Literal, "led Israel to sin" at Balanced, "led Israel into sin" at Readable. Later uses refer back here.

source.text: וַתָּ֨קָם֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת יָרָבְעָ֔ם וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ וַתָּבֹ֣א תִרְצָ֑תָה הִ֛יא בָּאָ֥ה בְסַף־הַבַּ֖יִת וְהַנַּ֥עַר מֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose [the] wife of Jeroboam and went and came to Tirzah; she [was] coming in the threshold of the house, and the boy died.

en.L: And the wife of Jeroboam arose and went and came to Tirzah. She [was] coming to the threshold of the house, and the boy died.
en.B: Then Jeroboam's wife got up and left and came to Tirzah. As she was stepping over the threshold of the house, the boy died.
en.R: Jeroboam's wife got up and went back home to Tirzah. Just as she stepped through the doorway of the house, the boy died.

decisions.choice: Tirzah: the royal city of the northern kingdom at this time
decisions.reason: Jeroboam had first built up Shechem (12:25); by now the king lived at Tirzah, northeast of Shechem. It stayed the capital of the northern kingdom until Omri built Samaria (15:21, 33; 16:23-24).

decisions.choice: she was coming to the threshold, and the boy died: at the very moment
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the two events side by side. The death came exactly as Ahijah had said (verse 12).

decisions.choice: the doorway (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for "threshold".

source.text: וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ וַיִּסְפְּדוּ־ל֖וֹ כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּדְבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַד־עַבְדּ֖וֹ אֲחִיָּ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And they buried him and mourned for him all Israel, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke by [the] hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.

en.L: And they buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave Ahijah the prophet.
en.B: They buried him, and all Israel mourned for him, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Ahijah the prophet.
en.R: The people buried him, and everyone in Israel mourned for him. This happened just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, the prophet Ahijah.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Yahweh: the first part of the prophecy comes true
decisions.reason: Kings often notes that a prophet's word was fulfilled (12:15; 15:29; 16:12, 34). The boy's death and burial happen as Ahijah said (verses 12-13); the rest waits for 15:29.

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through, by means of
decisions.reason: Yahweh speaks through his prophet as an agent: the "hand" is the one who carries out the act.

decisions.choice: his slave Ahijah (Literal); his servant Ahijah (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The rule for this word when used of Yahweh's prophets, as with "my servant David" (verse 8).

source.text: וְיֶ֨תֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יָֽרָבְעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִלְחַ֖ם וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מָלָ֑ךְ הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, behold they [are] written in [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Israel.

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, look, they [are] written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel.
en.B: The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fought and how he reigned, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.
en.R: Everything else Jeroboam did, the wars he fought and the way he ruled, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: a royal record, now lost
decisions.reason: This was an official record of the northern kingdom, a kind of court chronicle, which the writer of Kings used and pointed readers to. It is not the biblical book of Chronicles. Kings cites a "book of the acts of Solomon" (11:41) and, for the southern kingdom, a book of the kings of Judah (verse 29). None of these books has survived.

decisions.choice: the matters of Jeroboam: his deeds and the events of his reign
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word means words, matters or affairs. In this formula it means what the king did and what happened in his reign.

decisions.choice: how he fought: wars not told here
decisions.reason: Kings mentions war between Jeroboam and Rehoboam (verse 30) and with Abijam (15:7), but gives no details. 2 Chronicles 13:2-20 tells of one battle.

decisions.choice: the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel (Balanced); the history of the kings of Israel (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this source formula throughout Kings, opening with "The rest of the acts of" at Balanced and "Everything else ... did" at Readable. Here the Hebrew says "look, they are written" rather than asking "Are they not written?" (verse 29); Balanced and Readable state both as plain statements.

source.text: וְהַיָּמִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָלַ֣ךְ יָרָבְעָ֔ם עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֖יִם שָׁנָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ נָדָ֥ב בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And the days which reigned Jeroboam [were] twenty and two years; and he lay down with his fathers, and reigned Nadab his son in his place.

en.L: And the days that Jeroboam reigned [were] twenty-two years; and he lay down with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Jeroboam reigned twenty-two years. Then he rested with his ancestors, and his son Nadab became king in his place.
en.R: Jeroboam ruled as king for twenty-two years. Then he died, and his son Nadab became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The formula Kings uses for the death of a king (2:10; 11:43; verse 31). It speaks of death as lying down to rest and joining those who went before. Here it does not name the burial.

decisions.choice: Nadab his son reigned in his place: the reign that ends the house of Jeroboam
decisions.reason: Nadab reigned two years before Baasha killed him and the whole house of Jeroboam, as Ahijah had said (15:25-30; verse 14).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula is worded the same way at each level throughout Kings (2:10).

source.text: וּרְחַבְעָם֙ בֶּן־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וְאַחַ֣ת שָׁנָה֩ רְחַבְעָ֨ם בְּמָלְכ֜וֹ וּֽשֲׁבַ֨ע עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֣ה׀מָלַ֣ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֗ם הָ֠עִיר אֲשֶׁר־בָּחַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה לָשׂ֨וּם אֶת־שְׁמ֥וֹ שָׁם֙ מִכֹּל֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נַעֲמָ֖ה הָעַמֹּנִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah; a son of forty and one year[s was] Rehoboam in his reigning, and seventeen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem, the city which chose Yahweh to put his name there from all [the] tribes of Israel; and [the] name of his mother [was] Naamah the Ammonite.

en.L: And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam [was] a son of forty-one years when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name there. And the name of his mother [was] Naamah the Ammonite.
en.B: Rehoboam son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had chosen from among all the tribes of Israel as the place for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
en.R: Solomon's son Rehoboam was king in Judah. He became king at the age of forty-one, and he ruled for seventeen years in Jerusalem. Out of all the tribes of Israel, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had chosen this city as the place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would be worshiped. Rehoboam's mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.

decisions.choice: the opening formula for a king of Judah
decisions.reason: From here on Kings opens each reign with a set pattern. For the kings of Judah it gives the king's age when he became king, the length of his reign, the city where he reigned and his mother's name, and then a verdict on his reign (verse 22). Rehoboam's reign was first told in chapter 12; this formula returns to it after the story of Jeroboam.

decisions.choice: his mother was Naamah the Ammonite: the queen mother
decisions.reason: The kings of Judah are listed with their mothers, who held a place of honor at court (2:19; 15:13). Naamah came from Ammon, east of the Jordan. Since Rehoboam was forty-one when Solomon died after a forty-year reign (11:42), she was married to Solomon before he became king. She is one of the foreign wives of 11:1, and the next verses show Judah following foreign ways of worship.

decisions.choice: the city that Yahweh had chosen to put his name there: Jerusalem, the place of the temple
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy speaks of the one place Yahweh would choose to put his name (Deuteronomy 12:5, 11), and Kings names Jerusalem as that place (8:16, 29; 11:13, 36). The reminder sets Judah's worship at the chosen city against the high places described next.

decisions.choice: a son of forty-one years: forty-one years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years (2 Samuel 5:4).

decisions.choice: Rehoboam ... was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years
decisions.reason: The wording kept for the accession formula throughout Kings. Readable states the meaning of "to put his name there" (m3) as the place where Yahweh would be worshiped.

source.text: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוּדָ֛ה הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיְקַנְא֣וּ אֹת֗וֹ מִכֹּל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ אֲבֹתָ֔ם בְּחַטֹּאתָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָֽאוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And did Judah the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh, and they provoked him to jealousy more than all that did their fathers with their sins which they sinned.

en.L: And Judah did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they provoked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to jealousy more than all that their fathers had done, with their sins that they sinned.
en.B: Judah did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. By the sins they committed they stirred up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} jealousy more than all their ancestors had done.
en.R: The people of Judah did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil. Their sins made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} more jealous and angry than anything their ancestors had done.

decisions.choice: Judah did the evil: the people, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "Rehoboam did the evil", which matches the usual verdict on a king. The Hebrew blames the people of Judah as a whole, and the plural verbs that follow ("they provoked") agree with it. The account of the reign in 2 Chronicles 12:1, 14 speaks of both the king and the people. The Hebrew reading is followed.

decisions.choice: provoked him to jealousy: Yahweh's demand for undivided loyalty
decisions.reason: Yahweh's jealousy is the rightful claim of a husband or covenant partner who will not share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5; 34:14; Deuteronomy 32:16, 21). Worship of other gods stirs it up.

decisions.choice: the verdict: did evil in the sight of Yahweh
decisions.reason: Each reign in Kings is judged by this measure: did the king and people do what was right in Yahweh's sight, or what was evil? Judges uses the same words for Israel's turning away (Judges 2:11; 3:7).

decisions.choice: did what was evil in the sight of the LORD (Balanced); did what the LORD said was evil (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this verdict throughout the historical books.

decisions.choice: more jealous and angry (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "angry" so that "jealous" is not heard as petty envy (m2).

source.text: וַיִּבְנ֨וּ גַם־הֵ֧מָּה לָהֶ֛ם בָּמ֥וֹת וּמַצֵּב֖וֹת וַאֲשֵׁרִ֑ים עַ֚ל כָּל־גִּבְעָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה וְתַ֖חַת כָּל־עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And built also they for themselves high places and standing stones and Asherah poles on every hill high and under every tree luxuriant.

en.L: And they also built for themselves high places and standing stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
en.B: They also built for themselves high places, standing stones and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
en.R: They built hilltop shrines for themselves. They set up stone pillars and poles used to worship Asherah on every high hill and under every large, leafy tree.

decisions.choice: high places, standing stones and Asherah poles: places and objects of worship
decisions.reason: High places were local shrines with altars, often on hills (3:2). Standing stones were upright stones set up as sacred markers, which the law ordered Israel to break down when they were used in Canaanite worship (Exodus 23:24; Deuteronomy 16:22). Asherah poles: see verse 15.

decisions.choice: on every high hill and under every leafy tree: the places where the nations worshiped
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 12:2 commands Israel to destroy the places where the nations served their gods "on the high mountains and on the hills and under every leafy tree". Judah now builds such places for itself. The phrase is used again of this worship (2 Kings 16:4; 17:10).

decisions.choice: they also: Judah as well as Israel
decisions.reason: Judah too, not only the northern kingdom of verses 15-16, turned to these forms of worship.

decisions.choice: hilltop shrines, stone pillars, poles used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in these books.

source.text: וְגַם־קָדֵ֖שׁ הָיָ֣ה בָאָ֑רֶץ עָשׂ֗וּ כְּכֹל֙ הַתּוֹעֲבֹ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ הוֹרִ֣ישׁ יְהוָ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And also male cult prostitute was in the land; they did according to all the abominations of the nations which dispossessed Yahweh from before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And there were also male cult prostitutes in the land. They did according to all the abominations of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: There were even male shrine prostitutes in the land. The people did all the detestable things of the nations that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had driven out ahead of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: There were even men in the land who served as prostitutes at the shrines. The people did all the disgusting things that the nations had done before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} drove them out of the land for the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: male cult prostitutes: men attached to the shrines, probably for sexual rites
decisions.reason: The word (qadesh) means "consecrated one", a man set apart for a shrine. The law forbids it alongside the female form, which is used for a prostitute (Deuteronomy 23:18-19; Genesis 38:21-22). It is usually taken to mean men who served as prostitutes in the worship of other gods. Some think the word means men who served at the shrines in other ways, and that a sexual role is less certain. The singular here stands for a whole class of people. Later kings of Judah remove them (15:12; 22:47; 2 Kings 23:7).

decisions.choice: abominations: practices Yahweh detests
decisions.reason: The word is used for what is utterly offensive to Yahweh, especially the worship and customs of the Canaanite nations (Deuteronomy 18:9-12; 20:18).

decisions.choice: the nations Yahweh drove out before Israel: Judah repeats the sins for which the land was taken from them
decisions.reason: The nations lost the land because of these practices (Leviticus 18:24-28; Deuteronomy 9:4-5). If Judah does the same, it faces the same end.

decisions.choice: male cult prostitutes (Literal); male shrine prostitutes (Balanced); men who served as prostitutes at the shrines (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Deuteronomy 23:18, and the same at 15:12 and 22:47. Literal adds the plural, since the singular stands for a group (m1).

decisions.choice: abominations (Literal); detestable things (Balanced); disgusting things (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use words more common today for things that are deeply offensive.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֖ית לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֑ם עָלָ֛ה שִׁישַׁ֥ק מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was in the year the fifth of King Rehoboam, came up Shishak king of Egypt against Jerusalem.

en.L: And it happened in the fifth year of King Rehoboam [that] Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
en.B: In King Rehoboam's fifth year, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem.
en.R: In the fifth year that Rehoboam was king, Shishak, the king of Egypt, attacked Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Shishak king of Egypt: the pharaoh Sheshonq I
decisions.reason: Shishak is the Egyptian king Sheshonq I, who founded a new line of kings. He had given Jeroboam shelter when he fled from Solomon (11:40). His own inscription at the temple of Karnak in Egypt lists many towns in Judah and Israel that his army attacked, a campaign usually dated about 925 BC. 2 Chronicles 12:2-12 tells this attack more fully.

decisions.choice: Shishak: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) spell the name slightly differently; the form marked to be read aloud (qere) is Shishak, as in 11:40. The person is the same.

decisions.choice: in the fifth year of King Rehoboam: the attack follows Judah's sins
decisions.reason: The story places the invasion straight after the account of Judah's sins (verses 22-24). 2 Chronicles 12:2, 5 says it plainly: Shishak came because the people had been unfaithful to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: attacked Jerusalem (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Came up against" means came to attack; Jerusalem lies in the hills, so an army from Egypt "came up" to it.

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־אֹצְר֣וֹת בֵּית־יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת־אֽוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְאֶת־הַכֹּ֖ל לָקָ֑ח וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת־כָּל־מָגִנֵּ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took [the] treasures of [the] house of Yahweh and [the] treasures of [the] house of the king, and the all he took; and he took all [the] shields of the gold which made Solomon.

en.L: And he took the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the treasures of the house of the king; he took everything. And he took all the shields of gold that Solomon had made.
en.B: He carried off the treasures of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and those of the king's palace. He took everything, even all the gold shields Solomon had made.
en.R: He carried off the treasures from the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and from the king's palace. He took everything. He even took all the gold shields that Solomon had made.

decisions.choice: the treasures of the house of Yahweh and of the king's house: the wealth stored in temple and palace
decisions.reason: Both the temple and the palace held treasuries, filled with the gifts David and Solomon had dedicated (7:51). This is the first of several times Kings records them being emptied, by plunder or to pay off an enemy (15:18; 2 Kings 12:19; 18:15-16).

decisions.choice: the shields of gold that Solomon had made: the display shields of 10:16-17
decisions.reason: Solomon made two hundred large shields and three hundred small ones of hammered gold and placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon (10:16-17). They were a sign of his splendor. Five years after his death they are gone.

decisions.choice: he took everything: the plunder was complete
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "everything" first for emphasis. 2 Chronicles 12:9 repeats the list.

decisions.choice: the king's palace (Balanced, Readable); the temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same Hebrew word "house" is used for the king's palace and for Yahweh's temple, as in 3:1. Balanced keeps "house" for Yahweh's.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ רְחַבְעָם֙ תַּחְתָּ֔ם מָגִנֵּ֖י נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְהִפְקִ֗יד עַל־יַד֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרָצִ֔ים הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים פֶּ֖תַח בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And made King Rehoboam in their place shields of bronze, and he entrusted [them] on [the] hand of [the] commanders of the runners, the ones keeping [the] entrance of [the] house of the king.

en.L: And King Rehoboam made in their place shields of bronze, and he entrusted [them] to the hand of the commanders of the runners, who kept the entrance of the house of the king.
en.B: King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them and entrusted them to the commanders of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the king's palace.
en.R: So King Rehoboam made shields of bronze to take their place. He put them in the care of the commanders of the guard, the soldiers who guarded the entrance to the king's palace.

decisions.choice: shields of bronze in their place: the glory of Solomon's reign is gone
decisions.reason: Bronze takes the place of gold. The court keeps up the show, but what was golden in Solomon's day is now only bronze.

decisions.choice: the runners: the king's guard
decisions.reason: The "runners" were royal guards who ran before the king's chariot and kept watch at his palace (1 Samuel 22:17; 2 Samuel 15:1; 1 Kings 1:5). Their commanders were officers of the guard.

decisions.choice: the runners (Literal); the guard (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what the runners were (m2), as 1 Samuel 22:17 does at Balanced. "Commanders" is kept at every level, as for military leaders elsewhere.

source.text: וַיְהִ֛י מִדֵּי־בֹ֥א הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה יִשָּׂאוּם֙ הָֽרָצִ֔ים וֶהֱשִׁיב֖וּם אֶל־תָּ֥א הָרָצִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was as often as went the king [into the] house of Yahweh, carried them the runners, and they returned them to [the] guardroom of the runners.

en.L: And it happened, as often as the king went into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the runners carried them, and they brought them back to the guardroom of the runners.
en.B: Whenever the king went into the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the guards carried the shields, and afterward they brought them back to the guardroom.
en.R: Every time the king went to the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the guards carried the shields in front of him. Then they took them back to the guards' room.

decisions.choice: the runners carried them: the shields were for ceremony
decisions.reason: The shields were carried in procession when the king went up to the temple, and then stored away. They were for display, not for battle.

decisions.choice: the guardroom: a chamber where the guards were stationed
decisions.reason: The word means a room or chamber, here one used by the guards, where the shields were kept (Ezekiel 40:7 uses it for the guardrooms of the temple gate).

decisions.choice: the runners (Literal); the guards (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 27. Balanced does not repeat "of the guards" after "guardroom".

decisions.choice: in front of him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the shields were carried in procession before the king (m1).

source.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י רְחַבְעָ֖ם וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא־הֵ֣מָּה כְתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Rehoboam and all that he did, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of the kings of Judah?

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Rehoboam and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?
en.B: The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.
en.R: Everything else Rehoboam did is written in the history of the kings of Judah.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah: the royal record of Judah
decisions.reason: This is the court chronicle of the southern kingdom, alongside the one for Israel (verse 19). It has not survived, and it is not the biblical book of Chronicles.

decisions.choice: are they not written ...?: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: The question form points the reader to the source for more. It means "they are written there". This is the usual form of the formula in Kings; verse 19 uses "look" instead.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The question form stays at Literal and becomes a statement at Balanced and Readable, as for every use of this formula in Kings. The source's name is worded as in verse 19.

source.text: וּמִלְחָמָ֨ה הָיְתָ֧ה בֵין־רְחַבְעָ֛ם וּבֵ֥ין יָרָבְעָ֖ם כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And war was between Rehoboam and between Jeroboam all the days.

en.L: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days.
en.B: There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.
en.R: Rehoboam and Jeroboam were at war with each other the whole time they were kings.

decisions.choice: war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam: continued hostility along the border
decisions.reason: Yahweh had forbidden Rehoboam to fight to win back the north (12:21-24). This does not seem to be the full war he planned then, but ongoing fighting and raids between the two kingdoms. The same is said of Abijam and of Asa (15:6-7, 16).

decisions.choice: all the days: throughout their reigns
decisions.reason: "All the days" means all the time both of them were king.

decisions.choice: the whole time they were kings (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states what "all the days" refers to (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֨ב רְחַבְעָ֜ם עִם־אֲבֹתָ֗יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֤ר עִם־אֲבֹתָיו֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ נַעֲמָ֖ה הָעַמֹּנִ֑ית וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲבִיָּ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Rehoboam with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in [the] city of David; and [the] name of his mother [was] Naamah the Ammonite; and reigned Abijam his son in his place.

en.L: And Rehoboam lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David. And the name of his mother [was] Naamah the Ammonite. And Abijam his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Rehoboam rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite. His son Abijam became king in his place.
en.R: Rehoboam died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. Rehoboam's mother was named Naamah the Ammonite. His son Abijam became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as in verse 20 and 2:10. Here the burial follows: Rehoboam was laid in the royal tombs in the City of David, as David and Solomon were (2:10; 11:43).

decisions.choice: the name of his mother was Naamah the Ammonite: repeated from verse 21 on purpose
decisions.reason: The mother's name normally comes only in the opening formula of a reign. Its repetition here is unusual. It may have been repeated to stress that the king whose reign led Judah astray was the son of an Ammonite mother (11:1-2). The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: Abijam: the name of Rehoboam's son in Kings
decisions.reason: Kings calls him Abijam (15:1-8); 2 Chronicles 12:16 and 13:1 call him Abijah. He is not Jeroboam's son Abijah of verse 1.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died and was buried with his ancestors
decisions.reason: The death formula as worded throughout Kings (2:10). Balanced says "buried with them" to avoid repeating "ancestors".
